approach.method_basis: The Parent generates new molecular graphs by breeding and editing molecules that have already been scored in the current session. A Gaussian-process preference model uses count fingerprints and every strict pair of accepted scores to rank the fresh offspring. All comparisons receive the same weight, with their combined weight fixed to the older sparse graph. A deterministic mode fit and full Laplace covariance supply correlated function draws for selection; an inherited stall rule restricts eligible offspring by predicted mean. Actual raw scores still control survival and breeding. Complete comparisons improved ordinary paid ordering, but useful gain and final scores fell.
approach.novelty: Give each existing comparison a fixed share of the same total likelihood weight proportional to its observed raw-score gap. This adds magnitude-sensitive loss weighting while preserving the complete graph, prior and sampled search host. The hypothesis is that spending more loss weight on large observed gaps will improve gap-weighted ordering of later paid choices and may improve useful gain. The frozen sibling list is empty; the earlier sparse and uniform-complete variants changed which comparisons were present, whereas this variant changes their relative influence using score magnitudes.

observed_bottleneck: The one limiting behavior is weak magnitude-sensitive ordering after complete comparison coverage already repaired part of ordinary ordering. Actual code Parent n-b37d60f71872 uses a uniform E_old/M likelihood weight and has complete Search macro0.47969672018590265 with population seed SD0.0576715946432145; its paired mean versus sparse n-aaeb1a1ac082 is-0.025961675493073322 and versus formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is-0.12733359602522829. Its three actual summary.json and run.log files report all fifteen sessions complete; the scheduler warning in run.log did not prevent those reported completions. nodes/n-b37d60f71872/analysis.json records435 stationary fits,2438 changed purchased identities versus same-state sparse, ordinary ordering12260/19544 versus12026/19544, and worse late ordering and endpoints. The Parent coverage mechanism remains confirmed and its sparse predecessor refutation remains intact. The frozen policy/scratch/search_policy-9d59a945162f/gap-ordering-audit.json and our independently recomputed policy/scratch/r0063-01-improve-L01/parent-audit.json join4350 paid rows to the original trajectory identities/scores and recover19544 within-announcement strict pairs. Equal-session gap-weighted ordering is0.7144253609910537 active,0.6970377469995744 sparse and0.7856437557465344 raw GP; active trails raw in13/15 cells. The owned per-cell audits audit-seed-N-task.json name and hash every original task log, trajectory, run.log, summary and frozen policy audit. Arithmetic on actual accepted refit scores shows nonuniform gaps in435/435 fits, but no weighted model has been trained or evaluated in this audit. The measured error gap supports a specific test of importance weighting; it does not establish discarded magnitude as the cause of endpoint loss. Parent source nodes/n-b37d60f71872/optimize.py shows scalar weighting consistently enters objective, gradient and Hessian and identifies the bounded implementation seam.

adoptions.applicability: The actual Parent successfully executed435 complete comparison fits and provides the inference seam. The source justifies the inherited model structure, not this new raw-gap weighting, dependent preference count, molecular task transfer or endpoint benefit.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Probit comparison likelihood under a Gaussian-process prior and mode/Laplace predictive inference, already implemented by the Parent.

deviations.adopted_setting: All strict pairs are derived from the current session purchased raw scores, with fixed normalized raw-gap power weights summing to the inherited E_old; count-Tanimoto prior and numeric settings remain the actual Parent values.
deviations.paper_setting: A GP preference model conditions on pairwise preference observations.
deviations.reason: This is the frozen magnitude-sensitive weighting hypothesis on a measured Parent. Pairs are dependent transformations of the same labels, and the source supplies no independent-observation or calibration guarantee for the adaptation.

adoptions.implementation_change: Retain LocalPreferencePosterior zero-start whitened Newton and full Laplace prediction; consistently insert the fixed per-edge raw-gap weights into fit_active, map_quantities and trial_objective.

adoptions.applicability: The complete Parent improves ordinary ordering yet loses useful gain, and the frozen paid-label audit exposes a remaining magnitude-sensitive error gap. Cost sensitivity motivates this specific test but does not diagnose the cause or promise better final Top-1.
adoptions.borrowed_element: The distinction between counting pair-order mistakes and weighting their decision cost.

deviations.adopted_setting: A fixed raw-gap composite probit likelihood, recomputed once per real refit, with analytic derivatives and unchanged total evidence mass. No dynamic ranking discount, logistic learner, LambdaRank implementation, NDCG optimization or new dataset.
deviations.paper_setting: LambdaRank uses rank-metric changes such as NDCG differences to weight pair movements in a ranking learner.
deviations.reason: Only the mistake-count versus cost distinction is borrowed. The actual raw-gap rule is the campaign hypothesis fixed by this ticket, not a claim to reproduce the source algorithm or directly optimize final Top-1.

adoptions.implementation_change: Weight the existing negative probit pair likelihood and its exact gradient/Hessian by E_old*abs(raw score difference)/sum(abs(raw score difference)); assess equal-session gap-weighted paid ordering separately from ordinary ordering.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse only the two relevant sources from frozen search-policy-r63-observed-model-obstacles; no new search or query is claimed here (queries records none). Retain the measured Parent probit/Laplace machinery and adapt only comparison influence using the exact raw-gap rule. Internal evidence supports a testable opportunity, not a known training benefit. The immutable review contains the original actual queries. Its source manifest reports the Burges PDF was browsed but local archival retrieval returned403, so no local Burges raw bytes or renewed source verification is claimed. This review neither reopens the sparse refutation nor converts the complete Parent coverage confirmation into an endpoint claim.

sources.applicability: The model is already implemented and measured. Keep its inference, explicitly changing fixed pair weights from accepted cardinal gaps; the paper does not establish the proposed weighting or independent labels.
sources.finding: A probit pairwise likelihood under a GP prior admits MAP/Laplace predictive inference.
sources.title: Preference Learning with Gaussian Processes (Chu and Ghahramani, ICML 2005)

sources.applicability: Motivates a cost-sensitive comparison question after improved ordinary accuracy failed to improve endpoints. Adopt the distinction only: fixed raw-gap probit weighting is not the source algorithm, dynamic rank discount or direct Top-1 optimization.
sources.finding: Counting pairwise errors can disagree with a ranking utility; LambdaRank weights pair movements by their change in a ranking metric.
sources.title: From RankNet to LambdaRank to LambdaMART: An Overview (Burges, MSR-TR-2010-82)

hypothesis: Modify only the complete comparison loss of code Parent n-b37d60f71872. At each original chronological accepted-archive refit enumerate exactly its existing strict winner/loser pairs, omitting exact raw-score ties and preserving canonical feature aliases. Let M be the strict-pair count, E_old the same inherited non-tied nearest-predecessor count, g_e=abs(y_w-y_l) from accepted current-session RAW scores, and G=sum_e g_e. For positive E_old and G fix w_e=E_old*g_e/G once per refit. Use log likelihood sum_e w_e*logPhi(f_w-f_l), with the same nonnegative weights in the gradient and Hessian. All strict pairs remain and total mass remains E_old. This introduces cardinal-gap influence into a dependent power/composite likelihood, not new independent preference labels, raw-score regression, learned task scales or calibrated cardinal utilities. M=0, G=0 or E_old=0 uses the inherited explicit prior. Retain unit count-kernel prior, unit probit difference/noise interpretation, zero-start whitened bounded Newton MAP and full Laplace prediction; keep all downstream sampling, utility wrapper, mask and raw-score feedback laws. Redistribution predicts improved equal-session gap-weighted paid ordering against same-state uniform-complete inference; score benefit is a separate empirical question.

finding_summary.headline: Gap weighting executes but fails its ordering test; ordinary accuracy and late progress worsen
finding_summary.insights:
The failure is scientific, not an integration failure: the prescribed weights entered the probit objective, its derivatives, full Laplace predictions and actual sampled decisions. The registered remedy therefore fails on the complete purchased-label panel even though it beats the older sparse model. Comparing its 75.35% accuracy with the actual Parent’s 71.44% would hide this result because those models purchased different trajectories; the uniform model reaches 75.63% on the Child’s same labels. Borrowed probit/Laplace inference operated, and the borrowed distinction between error count and decision cost was implemented, but fixed raw-gap power weighting did not deliver its predicted benefit. This adaptation is not LambdaRank, calibrated raw utility or direct Top-1 optimization. It does not undo the earlier complete-coverage result or decide the future of preference learning.

The trajectories also expose a search limitation beyond the loss weights. The weak second docking session reached its best value, 0.02886, at optimizer ordinal 25, then made no further incumbent progress; all 145 late molecules remained above fifty heavy atoms. Other sessions reached compact, much stronger families. Across tasks the large-molecule tail grew from 488 to 648 purchases, while fragment-excluded within-session similarity rose from 0.27874 to 0.32635 despite broad aggregate scaffold counts. This supports a diagnosis of sustained refinement and expansion within some selected families, rather than a general lack of ring-building ability. A different observation/ranking model could address the remaining same-paid ordering deficit; a proposal or search scheme capable of coherent scaffold/linker remodeling could address family dependence. The evidence does not establish which is causal or promise that either would improve endpoints. Mean versus covariance effects, alternative adaptive trajectories and unpurchased opportunities remain unresolved. These descriptive chemistry patterns justify no universal size cutoff.
finding_summary.results: All 435 active fits converged, redistributed the intended likelihood mass and changed 1,120 actual purchases relative to uniform weighting on the same states. There were no failed fits, missing predictions or incomplete sessions. Yet the primary equal-session gap-weighted ordering accuracy fell from 75.6277% to 75.3481%, a decrease of 0.2797 percentage points; ten of fifteen cells worsened. This meets the registered scientific falsifier. Ordinary ordering also fell, from 65.9208% to 63.5554%, across 19,531 purchased non-tied pairs. The early gap-weighted difference was positive, but late ordering fell by 3.6305 points. The raw-score GP remained higher at 81.5689% on the same paid labels. Actual full incumbent gain fell from 4.06807 to 4.01169 and late gain from 1.41761 to 0.99248. Endpoint mean fell from 0.47970 to 0.47594; paired seed-average changes were +0.02676, -0.06401 and +0.02597. Six of fifteen endpoints improved, nine worsened, and seed dispersion increased from 0.05767 to 0.09943. The formal Anchor mean was 0.60703, so the separate +0.002 target was not attained. Child task-safety evidence was not supplied.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families, with seed-dependent oversized assemblies, reactive heteroatom decorations and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Complete paired Search evidence is available for n-ee7e0123f8c3 and code Parent n-b37d60f71872: all five tasks and seeds 0/1/2, with 290 accepted optimizer molecules per cell and 4,350 per node. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectories were read; no paths or paired cells are missing. Initial records are excluded from the following counts. These are accepted, evaluated structures; rejected proposals and unpurchased pools are not represented. Child output spans 1 to 120 heavy atoms, with median 31 versus Parent 27. Ring-bearing/aromatic-bearing counts are 4,301/4,086, consistent with the digest ring-text rates 0.9816 to 0.9954. The generator already makes fused, bridged, saturated and aromatic rings, amines, amides, nitriles, ethers and carbonyl heterocycles. Across the full panels, Child/Parent counts below six heavy atoms are 42/53, below twelve are 80/85, and above fifty are 648/488. The output includes recognizable medicinal fragments but also repeated decorated assemblies and uncommon local bonds: N-halogen 222/190, O-halogen 411/134, S-halogen 116/12, peroxide 331/132, and acyl halide 6/5. These overlapping structural flags are not measured instability or synthetic-accessibility scores. There are 1,862/1,881 distinct nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1,209/1,213 generic scaffolds. Broad aggregate diversity coexists with concentrated families within individual sessions. Equal-cell mean pairwise Morgan Tanimoto after excluding molecules below twelve heavy atoms is 0.3263521011/0.2787411687; this compares within-session pairs, not pairs across tasks. All digest stereocentre-text rates are zero. A common RDKit 2023.09.6 nonlegacy tetrahedral-center perception finds unassigned centers in 1,789/2,420 Child/Parent molecules and assigned centers in none; these are new matched-method counts, not reuse of an older Parent stereo audit. Evidence and definitions: policy/scratch/r0063-01-improve-L01/molecular/molecular-audit.json and its individually indexed audit-seed-N-task.json files, which cite all underlying run-relative inputs and hashes. Child input copies are byte-identical to the request-authorized staging trajectories; copying confers no new SMILES citation authority. Scores below are the observed trajectory values. Chemistry associations do not establish intervention activation, component contribution, synthesis feasibility, objective decomposition, or a causal explanation of endpoint differences.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly medium-sized aromatic amides and fused heteroaromatics: 870 paid structures, median 26 heavy atoms versus Parent 25, and no structures above fifty heavy atoms. Seed 0 favors two substituted phenyl rings joined through an enamine-containing chain and N-methyl amide, with nitrile and methoxy groups; its leading structure has 26 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. Seed 1 favors substituted indoles with a dicarbonyl amide; seed 2 favors fused pyrrolic/aromatic rings with an N-fluorinated hydrazide. The ring and aromatic text rates are 0.9885 and 0.9851. Ordinary amide/aryl connectivity is synthetically recognizable, while the N/O/S-halogen variants make the family questionable as a whole. Parent winners occupy more fused or bridged ring frameworks, and Child typed/generic scaffold counts fall to 274/144 from 423/252.
liabilities: The paid set contains 145 O-halogen, 100 S-halogen and 70 N-halogen structures. N-fluorohydrazides and heteroatom-halogen decorations warrant chemical review even when the graph parses.
Potential tetrahedral configurations remain unspecified when present; small zero-scoring fragments and occasional oversized aromatic combinations still occur.
missing_features: Consistent access to the favorable aromatic/amide architecture through ordinary heteroatom substitution is incomplete: many neighbors add O-halogen or S-halogen bonds. The observed highest seed-0 structure already shows that such bonds are not required for its score; improvement from removing them is untested.

The output offers fewer alternative scaffold arrangements than the Parent within this task. No particular absent target ring system or donor/acceptor requirement can be inferred from these trajectory scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 0 evaluation 241 reaches 0.47342796635814444 with the 26-heavy-atom nitrile/anilino-amide; replacing its aryl F with Cl at evaluation 296 leaves that score unchanged. Seed 1 evaluation 293 reaches 0.4178728841888079 and seed 2 evaluation 248 reaches 0.45348083502552267. Methane at seed 2 evaluation 43 and OF at seed 1 evaluation 18 both score zero; the much larger aromatic fusion at seed 0 evaluation 26 scores 5.274363423649259e-21. Thus the observed contrast favors a bounded, connected aromatic/polar architecture rather than indiscriminate growth or isolated fragments. The N-fluorinated seed-2 family scores well enough that the scalar values do not themselves demonstrate a chemical-stability preference. Parent maxima are 0.4745789978762495, 0.4463521672202675 and 0.43109245871924246 in seed order; the families differ and support descriptive comparison only.

per_task.generated_character: Heteroaromatic carbonyl scaffolds with many ether, ester, nitrile and ring-nitrogen substitutions dominate. The paid set has median 46 heavy atoms versus Parent 47, with 342/381 structures above fifty heavy atoms. Seed 1 makes a comparatively compact fused/bridged aromatic assembly carrying a nitrile and methoxy/fluoromethoxy groups. Seed 0 repeatedly concatenates coumarin-like and azaaromatic units through oxygen-rich linkers; its leading molecule has 113 heavy atoms and 17 aromatic rings. Seed 2 carries linked pyridyl and dicarbonyl heterocycle units with unsaturated chains and oxygen-halogen decorations. The large repeated assemblies have considerably less convincing practical synthetic plausibility than the compact seed-1 series. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 455/359 versus Parent 424/329.
liabilities: There are 270 peroxide-bearing and 137 O-halogen-bearing structures versus Parent 52 and 70. These counts overlap and do not prove which individual compounds are stable.

The combination of extensive aromatic repetition, many linkers and reactive oxygen connectivity makes purification, synthesis and molecular-property interpretation questionable; no synthetic route was evaluated.
missing_features: Reliable compact remodeling of the high-scoring heteroaromatic arrangements is missing from the repeated-assembly branch. The compact highest-scoring example demonstrates an available alternative to huge repeated units, without establishing any universal size limit.
Ordinary oxygen-linker alternatives are not consistently retained: peroxide and O-halogen variants become common. Their replacement is a chemical capability gap, with score benefit undetermined.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Ethane, methanol and fluorobenzene examples sit at the observed 0.5 floor. The compact 35-heavy-atom seed-1 evaluation 279 reaches 0.6104318131747081, while seed-0 evaluation 286 reaches 0.6083278922063275 with 113 heavy atoms; seed-2 evaluation 282 reaches 0.5920761864674313 with 55 heavy atoms. Elaborate heteroaromatic connectivity separates these from the simple fragments, but greater size does not monotonically increase score. All 145 late seed-0 structures exceed fifty heavy atoms, with late median 97, whereas seed 1 has late median 35. Published Parent bests contain 63, 41 and 76 heavy atoms in seed order; its seed-1 maximum 0.6253140905869468 is associated with another decorated heteroaromatic family. These observations do not reveal an obligatory missing target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The output splits into chemically different seed families. Seed 0 makes fluorinated diaryl structures with small carbon or nitrogen rings and exposed aminoalkyl chains. Its leading molecule has 28 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings and a small unsaturated carbocycle. Seed 2 favors diaryl alkenes with an aliphatic secondary amine, thiol/aniline and halogen decorations. Seed 1 instead expands an oxygen-rich polycyclic acetal family; its best graph has 118 heavy atoms, 19 rings and 33 unassigned potential tetrahedral centers. Across the task, median size is 34 versus Parent 25 and above-fifty counts are 294/100. The compact aminoalkyl/aromatic connectivity is recognizable chemistry, although strained-ring and reactive substituent variants occur. The giant acetal assemblies are far less convincing ordinary medicinal structures.
liabilities: Seed 2 retains O-Cl connectivity even in its high-scoring leading structure; the task contains 120 O-halogen molecules versus Parent 21.

The oxygen-rich large branch and small strained-ring variants require chemistry review. Potential stereochemistry is unassigned in 619 paid structures, and the leading seed-0 molecule has two unassigned potential tetrahedral centers.
missing_features: Consistent within-session access to compact amine-bearing ring/linker arrangements is missing from the oversized branch. Adding nitrogen indiscriminately would not address the observed architectural difference.

Defined configurations at the fluorinated saturated center and substituted small ring are absent in the leading seed-0 graph; the large acetal branch also lacks specified ring-junction stereochemistry. Whether stereochemical specification changes this objective is not measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact diamine-bearing seed-0 evaluation 262 scores 0.9537075088475077; seed-2 evaluation 279 scores 0.8678215294297158. By contrast, the sulfonyl-protected ring-nitrogen fragment at seed-0 evaluation 20 scores 0.00021169315013374197. The 118-heavy-atom oxygen-rich seed-1 evaluation 35 reaches only 0.02885837683273086, and all 145 late molecules from that seed remain above fifty heavy atoms. This association supports accessible amine-bearing, connected aromatic architectures over the observed protected-N fragments or giant oxygen-rich structures; it is not a receptor-binding explanation. Amines and saturated ring nitrogens are already accessible to this generator, so a global absence of basic centers would be incorrect. Parent winners are 23, 39 and 24 heavy atoms, at 0.9840608116477806, 0.18710087188665003 and 0.8724432739963158. The Child reproduces compact amine-rich families in some sessions while retaining a very different large family in another.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-sized carbonyl-containing polycycles dominate: median 32 heavy atoms versus Parent 31, with 859 of 870 molecules bearing a carbonyl and only seven above fifty heavy atoms. Seed 0 combines a fused aromatic dicarbonyl heterocycle with an unsaturated nitrogen ring; seed 1 makes a diaryl nitrogen-ring framework coupled by an exocyclic alkene to a larger N-methyl dicarbonyl ring; seed 2 links an azaaromatic bicycle to a tightly fused or bridged dicarbonyl nitrogen polycycle. The leading seed-1 graph has 34 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and two aromatic rings. These functional groups are familiar, but the ring fusion, exocyclic unsaturation and some bridged topologies leave synthetic plausibility uncertain. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 425/271 versus Parent 411/265, so ring and scaffold availability are substantial.
liabilities: Complex bridge and junction topology plus exocyclic alkene placement can make a valid graph difficult to realize; no route or conformational feasibility analysis is available.
473 paid molecules have unassigned potential tetrahedral centers. N-halogen, O-halogen and peroxide motifs occur even in this relatively less halogen-rich task.
missing_features: More coherent alternatives in ring size, fusion and linker placement remain a plausible coverage gap relative to the different Parent family. Aromatic rings, amines and carbonyls themselves are already abundant; the trajectories do not identify a specific absent pharmacophore.
Configuration is left unspecified when the generator creates stereogenic saturated ring junctions. This is an output-completeness gap rather than a demonstrated score requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading seed-1 evaluation 292 scores 0.22303309427262127; its closely related ring-expanded analog at evaluation 248 scores 0.21842181317576892. Seed-0 and seed-2 bests score 0.19512536527753646 and 0.20993628325309233. Methane scores zero, methanol 0.008773280079294957 and chloroethane 0.014932027335788824. The observed gradient favors assembled aromatic/polar heterocyclic topology over isolated fragments and distinguishes ring arrangement within a family. Parent seed-2 instead reaches 0.2467131287326799 with a less tightly bridged indole-containing dicarbonyl family; this supports a remaining architecture-coverage question, not an identified missing functional group or proof that more rings help.

per_task.generated_character: Fluorinated nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl heterocycles with compact aromatic or partially saturated ring systems dominate the upper-scoring output. Median size is 26 heavy atoms versus Parent 23; only five Child structures exceed fifty heavy atoms. Seed 0 retains a fused aromatic dicarbonyl core linked to a fluorinated azaaryl ring and fluorinated sidechains. Seed 1 includes N-F, cyclopropyl chloride and fluoromethoxy decorations. Seed 2 makes compact highly fused saturated/unsaturated nitrogen rings carrying N=O and fluoroalkyl groups; its leading graph has 27 heavy atoms and six perceived rings but no aromatic rings. Aromatic-text rate is 0.7678, lower than the other supplied tasks while ring-text rate remains 0.9828. Familiar carbonyl cores coexist with synthetically questionable peripheral bonds and ring topology.
liabilities: 89 structures contain N-halogen bonds and 124 contain N=O bonds, compared with Parent 73 and one. The N=O count is a structural match, not a toxicology prediction.
512 molecules contain unassigned potential tetrahedral centers; strained and tightly fused saturated ring arrangements add synthetic uncertainty even at moderate molecular size.
missing_features: Defined stereochemistry is absent from the new saturated fluorinated sidechains and ring junctions: the seed-0 best has one unassigned potential tetrahedral center and seed-2 best has six. No score comparison between assigned stereoisomers is available.

Chemically ordinary peripheral alternatives to N-F and N=O decorations are not consistently expressed while retaining the productive-sized carbonyl architecture. The observed scores do not demonstrate that removing those groups improves the objective, and they do not establish a missing basic-amine requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed-0 evaluation 294 scores 0.5925150983631181 with a saturated fluorinated sidechain; the closely related unsaturated-sidechain molecule at evaluation 285 scores 0.5215071312813091. Seed-1 evaluation 297 reaches 0.4052757109339809, and the nonaromatic seed-2 evaluation 284 reaches 0.5071831026658341. A large repeated dicarbonyl/aromatic assembly at seed-1 evaluation 15 scores 3.2416258040348776e-69, while the stripped-down core at seed-2 evaluation 298 scores 2.1524851942772288e-12. Thus the observed values favor a bounded, decorated polar/fluorinated architecture; neither maximizing aromaticity nor simple truncation explains the gradient. Parent bests are 22, 28 and 22 heavy atoms at 0.4288530685378449, 0.5434954401077301 and 0.35948486956814124. Different seed families remain, including reactive Parent variants, so the comparison does not establish a universal chemical improvement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ee7e0123f8c3 versus published code Parent n-b37d60f71872, under the frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, unchanged batch-ten profile and 290 accepted optimizer molecules per session. Full-panel Child/Parent molecule counts are N-halogen 222/190, O-halogen 411/134, S-halogen 116/12, peroxide 331/132 and acyl-halide 6/5. The categories overlap. The leading observed compact families include both ordinary carbon-bound halogens and unusual heteroatom-halogen decorations; the existing score evidence does not establish that the latter are necessary. Counts and definitions are in policy/scratch/r0063-01-improve-L01/molecular/molecular-audit.json. This is an association in generated chemistry, not attribution to the changed model.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain ordinary local functional-group connectivity while modifying otherwise useful ring and heteroatom frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs the capability to preserve a coherent scaffold while distinguishing carbon halogenation from N/O/S halogenation and offering ordinary linker or substituent alternatives to reactive connectivity. Those alternatives must be tested through permitted session feedback; a structural flag alone neither proves instability nor authorizes a blanket filter or a claimed score gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ee7e0123f8c3, compared with n-b37d60f71872 on the same complete frozen Search panel. Every digest stereocentre-text rate is zero. Common RDKit 2023.09.6 nonlegacy tetrahedral-center perception finds unassigned potential centers in 1,789 of 4,350 Child structures and 2,420 of 4,350 Parent structures, with assigned centers in none. A compact fluorinated leading structure carries one unassigned center, another leading aminoalkyl/aromatic structure carries two, and a large polycyclic acetal carries 33. These are newly recomputed matched-method descriptors; historical Parent stereo tallies using another perception method are not substituted. Source audit: policy/scratch/r0063-01-improve-L01/molecular/molecular-audit.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves configuration unspecified when it creates stereogenic sidechains, substituted small rings and saturated ring junctions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation needs to preserve or explicitly explore stereochemical assignments when constructing stereogenic molecular graphs, subject to canonical identity and the existing session budget. This is an observed structural-specification gap; the data contain no assigned-isomer comparison and establish no score benefit from resolving it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ee7e0123f8c3 versus n-b37d60f71872, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, identical accepted-molecule denominators. Child/Parent counts below six heavy atoms are 42/53, below twelve are 80/85, and above fifty are 648/488. Child size spans 1 to 120 heavy atoms. Two separate sessions have all 145 late molecules above fifty heavy atoms, while compact high-scoring families remain in other sessions. Global nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts remain broad at 1,862/1,209 versus 1,881/1,213; equal-cell fragment-excluded pairwise similarity is 0.3263521011 versus 0.2787411687. Broad global scaffolds therefore do not rule out local repetition. Definitions and all cell/phase records are preserved in policy/scratch/r0063-01-improve-L01/molecular/molecular-audit.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable control of coherent scaffold and linker remodeling across sessions, allowing both fragment collapse and repeated oversized assembly.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is controlled remodeling that retains useful neighboring chemistry while changing ring/linker organization, without repeatedly copying whole decorated units or reducing them to isolated fragments. Any task-agnostic intervention should preserve both size tails, cell-specific families, typed/generic scaffolds and fragment-excluded similarity as descriptive checks. These observations justify no universal size cutoff, component attribution or promised endpoint gain.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
